newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed near session highs on Friday as lacklustre trading was enlivened by long-awaited U.S. payrolls data.

The 10-year benchmark dipped sharply immediately after the announcement of a 250,000 increase in nonfarm payrolls in August (versus expected +244,000) and an unemployment rate of 5.1 percent (vs expected 5.3 percent).
But it soon gained ground. "It was hard to get the chance to buy on the dip," said one dealer. "The market seemed prepared to take up a higher level unless the figures were really bad."
Some dealers said the market had entered a new phase where stockpiles of cash would at last be invested to push bund futures and guilder bonds higher.

"There's an empty market on the upside...I think the next stop for the bund future will be 97.30," one dealer said. "The market is definitely going up. There's so much cash to invest yet and the market senses that."
Bund spreads were largely unchanged on the day. The 10-year benchmark guilder bond closed 10 basis points under the April 2006 bund and the long bond closed 20 basis points under the comparable bund.
